outcome: blame never presents attribution stronger than the threat model allows
acceptance: Degraded-isolation run: blame prints the VOID line (THREAT-MODEL Live setup wording) and exits non-zero or labels candidates VOID; blame takes --head ANCHOR and without it says 'consistent, not anchored'; tests for both
summary: ks blame now runs verify (VerifyReport fields: isolation, anchored, unanchored_reason, last_witnessed_seq) and prints that first; takes --head ANCHOR; unanchored says 'consistent, not anchored (reason)'; VOID (isolation degraded) prints the attribution-VOID line and labels candidates/suspect 'unattributed: isolation degraded' (exit stays OK). review:
[panel · changes] Attack re-run live (non-root sandbox, so both runs degraded): VOID run (--shared-uid) and plain run both print verify first, VOID line, candidates and suspect labelled 'unattributed: isolation degraded'; no head -> 'consistent, not anchored (no_anchor)'; valid --head -> 'anchored'; garbage --head -> exit 64; foreign run's anchor -> UNVERIFIED keyring_mismatch exit 3. Good. ONE BLOCKER vs outcome 'never presents attribution stronger than TM allows': on VOID the taint line still prints 'agents with tainted actions: billing, comms, compliance, crm, ...' unlabelled, i.e. per-agent attribution by agent_id on a run where agent_id is void (RT3b). Fix: label that list '(unattributed: isolation degraded)' under void, and extend test_blame_void_run_does_not_attribute to assert it. Minor: non-VOID unanchored path is tested only via monkeypatched isolation; acceptable.

[panel · done] Re-checked live on the --shared-uid VOID run: verify line first, VOID line, root candidates, suspect and the 'agents with tainted actions' list all carry '[unattributed: isolation degraded]'; exit 0.
